title: HD 303514 plate tests retain a recovery preference after exposure averaging and removal of whole time blocks
abstract: We test whether finite plate exposures and groups of plate errors change a published comparison of two HD 303514 orbital states. We join DASCH DR7 exposure metadata to 2,823 selected plates from 1889-1955. Flux integration gives weighted fit gains of 88.40 for the recovery state and 53.68 for the eclipse-loss state. The preference changes by only 0.0041 from instantaneous templates on the same records. Recovery remains preferred after removal of any one year, decade or plate series. Whole-year resampling gives a central 95 percent range of 12.88-58.72 for the full-shape advantage and 4.54-28.47 for timing alone. However, removal of the 20 records that favor recovery most leaves advantages of 0.20 and -1.54. Thus the test survives exposure averaging and time-block removal but has limited record-level redundancy. These are fixed-state sensitivity tests, not probabilities of eclipse loss. We include code, simulated histories, aggregate results, source hashes and an external retrieval recipe.

display.caption: Recovery preference after exposure averaging, whole-year resampling and adverse record removal. Positive values favor the recovery state. Resampling intervals are descriptive.
